title: Sampling distributions & CLT
examples: When do we use the standard error instead of the standard deviation?
What does the sampling distribution actually show us?
Can you explain the difference between the population mean and the sample mean?

explain.say: Today we learn about the sampling distribution of the mean. This distribution describes the means from many samples. We are looking at the distribution of sample means, not individual data points.

items: Focuses on sample means, not points

explain.say: If we take many random samples, each with the same size, their means will form a distribution. The mean of this distribution will be close to the true population mean. This is a key concept to understand.

The standard deviation of this sampling distribution is called the standard error. It tells us how much sample means are expected to vary. We calculate it by dividing the population standard deviation by the square root of the sample size.
For example, if the population standard deviation is ten, and our sample size is twenty-five, the standard error is ten divided by the square root of twenty-five. This equals two.

faq.q: What is the difference between standard deviation and standard error?
faq.a: Standard deviation measures spread in the original population data. The standard error measures the spread of the sample means themselves. It is always smaller than the standard deviation.
asks: What is the spread of sample means?
How do I calculate the variability of sample means?

faq.q: Does the sample size affect the standard error?
faq.a: Yes, the sample size is in the denominator of the standard error formula. As the sample size increases, the standard error gets smaller. This means sample means cluster closer to the true mean.
asks: How does sample size impact SE?

faq.q: Do I need the Central Limit Theorem for this?
faq.a: The Central Limit Theorem helps us know that the sampling distribution approaches a normal distribution. This is true even if the original population is not normal. This allows us to use normal calculations.
asks: When can I assume a normal distribution?
What does the CLT allow us to do?

faq.q: What is the mean of the sampling distribution?
faq.a: The mean of the sampling distribution of the sample means is equal to the true population mean. It does not change regardless of the sample size or distribution shape.
asks: Is the mean of sample means always $\mu$?
What is the expected value of $\bar{x}$?

faq.q: Can I use this if I don't know the population standard deviation?
faq.a: If you do not know the population standard deviation, you must use the sample standard deviation instead. You will then use a t-distribution instead of the z-distribution for calculations.
asks: Should I use t or z?

facts: The mean of the sampling distribution of the sample mean equals the population mean, $\mu$.
The standard error is calculated as the population standard deviation divided by the square root of the sample size.
The Central Limit Theorem states that the sampling distribution approaches normal as sample size increases.
When the population is normal, the sampling distribution is normal regardless of sample size.

quiz.say: If the population standard deviation is 15 and the sample size is 9, what is the standard error?
quiz.why: The standard error is the population standard deviation divided by the square root of the sample size, which is fifteen divided by three, equaling five.

wrong.0: This is incorrect because you forgot to account for the sample size in the calculation.
wrong.1: This is incorrect because you squared the standard deviation instead of taking the square root.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because you divided the standard deviation by the sample size, not its square root.

quiz.say: A sample mean is calculated from a sample of 100 students. If the population mean is 75, what is the expected mean of all such sample means?
quiz.why: The mean of the sampling distribution of the sample mean is always equal to the true population mean, which is seventy-five.

wrong.0: This is incorrect because you multiplied the population mean by the sample size.
wrong.2: This is incorrect because the sample size does not change the expected mean.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because you divided the population mean by the sample size.

quiz.say: If the population standard deviation is 20 and the sample size is 4, what is the standard error?
quiz.why: The standard error is twenty divided by the square root of four, which is twenty divided by two, resulting in ten.

wrong.0: This is incorrect because you ignored the effect of the sample size.
wrong.2: This is incorrect because you divided the standard deviation by four, not the square root of four.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because you squared the standard error calculation.
